messages:
pagerbot: P0 alert — gpu_queue_length > 15k for runtime-prod-us-west-2. 90th pct latency > 4s. Autoscaler attempted 6 scale actions in last 5m; 4 failed with placement errors. @maya you're oncall.

maya (sre): seeing it, joining. any direct customer reports?

beth (cust-success): got 2 emails from enterprise customers complaining about 503s for embedding jobs. escalated.

eric (eng-runtime): logs show a ton of 'NoSuitableNode' from the placement service. looks like autoscaler launched pods, scheduler couldn't bind due to MIG template mismatch and strict binpack policy.

sam (oncall): joining voice. quick checks: cluster gpu utilization is 62%, but free MIG slices are in many small fragments. queue growth -> autoscaler keeps failing, so queue keeps stacking.

lee (infra): confirmed — a recent MIG template rollout (yesterday) introduced a 2/3 slice profile for some node pools in us-west-2a and us-west-2b. other pools are 1/4 slices. The scheduler only allows exact match by default, so pods requesting 3-slice config can't land on 1/4 nodes and vice versa. result: lots of nodes partially free but unusable -> stranded capacity.

ashish (scheduler): also seeing binpack fragmentation in the logs: 'nodeFits=false reason=resourcesUnavailable:migSizeMismatch'. autoscaler attempts to create new nodes but scale quota for us-west-2 is at soft limit (account-level) and the create calls are throttled.

pagerbot: Incident started 2025-11-02T17:53:20Z. Paginated oncall list. Priority: P0.

maya (sre): immediate mitigations we can try — list and assign: 1) relax scheduler MIG strictness to allow fallback placement to compatible MIG (low-risk config change). 2) temporarily bump cloud GPU quota in us-west-2 (requires infra approval). 3) enable burstpool (pre-warmed spare capacity) and route new requests. 4) evict/scale down best-effort training queues. who can action 1 and 3 quickly?

eric (eng-runtime): I can flip a scheduler flag to allow 'compatible' matching instead of exact. deploying now. will post the exact kubectl to run.

lee (infra): I can request a temporary quota bump but that's likely >30m. meanwhile we can activate burstpool by toggling the burstpool policy for runtime-prod; doing that now.

sam (oncall): I'm going to identify low-priority jobs we can preempt. running query: `kubectl get pods -n training -l priority=best-effort -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.phase}\n'`

ashish (scheduler): i pushed config patch to scheduler: `MIGMatchPolicy: COMPATIBLE` (hot-reload). restarting scheduler pods one at a time.

pagerbot: scheduler restart job started (job-id: sr-484321).

sam (oncall): preempting 18 best-effort pods now (`kubectl delete --force ...`).

beth (cust-success): letting the two impacted customers know we're on it. will update Slack thread with timeline & mitigation so they can forward.

~ 8 minutes later ~

eric (eng-runtime): scheduler hotfix applied. autoscaler create attempts are now succeeding to bind in several cases. queue length down from 15.3k -> 6.1k. latency 90th down from 4.2s -> 1.8s.

lee (infra): burstpool activated. 12 pre-warmed GPUs added to runtime-prod. some traffic shifted to burstpool — token cost spike but customer impact reduces.

ashish (scheduler): still seeing ~2k queued due to fragmentation across AZs. plan: schedule a rolling repack (drain -> reprovision with uniform MIG template). need approval for disruptive repack window.

maya (sre): status check: customer 503s are dropping. beth please confirm with customers.

beth (cust-success): emailed both customers with update: "We routed traffic to pre-warmed capacity and applied a scheduler hotfix. We're monitoring; will share postmortem." They replied thanks and asked for ETA on full fix.

sam (oncall): next steps I'm taking now: 1) keep autoscaler in reactive mode, 2) set temporary scale-limit +20% to allow more nodes if quota approved, 3) start job to drain 30 fragmented nodes for consolidated reprovisioning tomorrow 0300 UTC.

eric (eng-runtime): note — we should also add a routing fallback in the control plane: model-quantized-1 (lower-capacity variant) in a different pool (cpu/gpu-mixed) can accept embedding requests during future degradations. I'm opening a feature ticket.

ashish (scheduler): quick config we rolled: added a compatibility matrix to MIG matcher: allow 2/3 <-> 1/4 migrange for fractional packing. will follow up with a migration plan.

~ 40 minutes later ~

eric (eng-runtime): queue stable ~2k and trending down. 90th latency stable at 1.3s. no new customer complaints in the last 20m.

maya (sre): declaring incident mitigation in place. will wait 1hr of stable metrics before demobilizing pager.

pagerbot: Incident mitigated (status: degraded). Auto-close disabled. Incident lead: maya (sre). Postmortem owner: eric (eng-runtime).

lee (infra): followups: 1) revert burstpool to normal policy after capacity normalizes, 2) coordinate MIG template rollback or mass reprovision with eng-runtime tomorrow, 3) request permanent quota increase for us-west-2.

ashish (scheduler): followups: 1) add more tolerant matching rules permanently, 2) add a continuously running fragmentation metric and alert when stranded capacity > 20%.

beth (cust-success): i'll send a customer update summary after we have the postmortem.

maya (sre): assigning action items in incident board. ETA for postmortem draft: 48h.

sam (oncall): adding brief runbook update: under "GPU MIG mismatch" add step: if scheduler returns migSizeMismatch, flip MIGMatchPolicy to COMPATIBLE and enable burstpool, then escalate to infra for quota.

pagerbot: Incident update logged to #incidents. CID: inc-20251102-484321.

(End of thread)
